The suggested fix to skip the 300ms throttle for fallback={null} sounds
like a great solution. If there is no visible fallback being displayed,
removing the delay would certainly improve the user experience and address
the issue described.

Please let us know if you need any assistance or further testing as you
implement this.


On Tue, Jun 16, 2026, 1:51 PM Hesam ***@***.***> wrote:

> *hesam-oxe* left a comment (react/react#36569)
> <https://github.com/react/react/issues/36569#issuecomment-4722227426>
>
> @Diyoncrz18 <https://github.com/Diyoncrz18> Great analysis!
>
> The "skip throttle for fallback={null}" approach seems like the
> most targeted fix — if there's no visible fallback, there's nothing
> to throttle for.
>
> I can implement this: check if Suspense fallback is null/undefined,
> and if so, skip the FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS delay.
>
> @andyticker <https://github.com/andyticker> Would this address your use
> case? If you use
> fallback={null} or no fallback prop, the component would render
> immediately when the lazy promise resolves.
>
> /assign
